newsitem.title: UK: No new French green rate now seen on Aug 1 - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: No new French green rate now seen on Aug 1 - HGCA.

text.p: A devaluation of the French green rate, previously predicted for August 1, is not now expected to take place, according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.
The French rate was earlier expected to be devalued because of relative franc weakness against other EU currencies, creating a negative 'Real Monetary Gap'.
However, devaluations are currently forecast for the Belgian, German, Dutch, Danish, Spanish, Portuguese and Austrian green rates on 1 August, the HGCA said.
And sterling is currently forecast to enter its fourth of a possible five confirmation periods ahead of a possible revaluation on 21 August 1997.

The HGCA prediction is based on official currency rates against the Ecu so far in a monitoring period which started on July 21. An element of uncertainty still remains, as the final rates will depend on currency moves between now and when Thursday's Ecu rates are calculated.
Green rates are used by the European Union to convert Ecus into the currencies of its member states in its Common Agricultural Policy.
